comments.author: Rebar Bot Nava
comments.body:
Root-cause findings (2026-11-21 PST, rebar-session-05f74084). There are 6 sub-causes, 3 of them product defects. Evidence: Windows JUnit run 44681457334, Windows probe run 44900309390, and local macOS runs with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL setting core.autocrlf=true. Local result: 2 of the 11 fail and 8 pass; the rest need Windows text mode.
1. PRODUCT: `rebar._store.gitutil.run_git` (and `_run_in_group`) passes str stdin with `text=True`. On Windows, Python's text-mode stdin rewrites every `\n` as `\r\n`, so every caller that pipes text to git sends CRLF. Probe run 44900309390 shows the effect: `update-index --index-info` fed that way records NO entries (bytes stdin records all 3 stages). Test: test_run_git_wrapper::test_str_input_is_forwarded_to_stdin (piped hash != file hash).
2. PRODUCT: `rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay.tier2` (tier2.py:225) writes `objects/info/alternates` with `open(..., "w")`. On Windows the line ends in `\r\n`, git keeps the `\r` in the path ("objects?"), the objects are not found, and `git reset --hard` exits 128. Tests: the 4 test_plan_replay_tier2 materialize tests.
3. PRODUCT (ops tooling): `infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py` main() refuses `scratch worktree is not clean` because `git status --porcelain` reports line-ending-only differences under core.autocrlf=true. This reproduces locally with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL autocrlf=true. Test: test_reclaim_bridge_history::test_unrelated_remote_ref_movement_does_not_fail_dry_run (the script exits 1 before its 2nd ls-remote, so the test's ref assertion fails).
4. TEST HARNESS: `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.extract_store_snapshot` uses `git archive`, which applies core.autocrlf, so extracted event files come out CRLF. This reproduces locally. Test: test_dc_store_copy_bounded_25e0::test_the_bounded_slice_still_carries_real_tickets_and_store_metadata.
5. CHECKOUT: the vendored, SHA-256-pinned files `tests/external/live_jira_dc/pycontribs-jira-LICENSE.txt` and `.github/schemas/gitlab-ci.schema.json` have no eol attribute, so a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true (the Git for Windows system default) converts them to CRLF and their pinned hashes no longer match. Tests: test_jira_dc_harness_shape, test_bridge_provider_wrappers, test_reconcile_workflow_lint.
6. TEST: test_mcp_publisher_pin::_verify pipes `"<sha>  <file>\n"` to `sha256sum -c` with text=True, and sha256sum sees `'mcp-publisher.tar.gz'$'\r'`.
Note: cause 1's mechanism (text-mode stdin) is also what breaks cold-censorable-armedcrab's unmerged-recovery fixture. That test helper is fixed under that ticket; the product run_git belongs here.

comments.author: Rebar Bot Nava
comments.body: Correction to finding 3 (reclaim_bridge_history). The macOS 'scratch worktree is not clean' reproduction is an artifact. The test passes an environment that replaces the whole env, so my GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL autocrlf config was dropped for the script's git while the worktree had been checked out CRLF; with the config visible, 'git status --porcelain' is clean (ls-files --eol shows i/lf w/crlf, porcelain ''). On Windows the cause is different and not line endings: the test injects the unrelated ref through a '#!/bin/sh' file named 'git' prepended to PATH. Windows CreateProcess never runs it (no .exe), so the ls-remote counter never fires, refs/heads/unrelated is never created, and the test's rev-parse exits 128. That is a POSIX-shell-stub defect (the posix-shell-stubs class, transhuman-wounded-pangolin's tests/_exe_stub.py helper), not CRLF. infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py has no line-ending defect on this evidence.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Discovered while triaging breezy-hogged-mastiff. The 11 entries of `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/crlf.args` belong to this bug. Root-cause evidence (Windows JUnit 44681457334, probe run 44900309390, local macOS runs under core.autocrlf=true) is in this ticket's comments. Depends on transhuman-wounded-pangolin for one test (sub-cause 6).

## Root cause (6 sub-causes; 2 in product code)
1. **Product contract: `gitutil.run_git` / `_run_in_group` pipe str stdin in text mode.** On Windows Python rewrites each `\n` as `\r\n`, so git receives CRLF. `hash-object --stdin` then hashes different bytes. No shipped caller is affected today: `reconciler/_ref_lock.py` already hashes bytes with `text=False`, and `_snapshot/delta_tree.py`'s checkout-index payload is NUL-separated. The fix makes `run_git`'s documented str-stdin contract platform-stable. The same translation makes `update-index --index-info` record nothing (probe run 44900309390), though no product caller does that today. Test: `test_run_git_wrapper::test_str_input_is_forwarded_to_stdin`.
2. **Product: `llm/evals/plan_replay/tier2.py` writes `objects/info/alternates` in text mode.** The `\r` stays in the path, the borrowed objects are not found, and `git reset --hard` exits 128. Tests: the 4 `test_plan_replay_tier2` materialize tests.
3. **Checkout: 2 SHA-256-pinned vendored files carry no eol attribute.** Git for Windows defaults to core.autocrlf=true, so they check out CRLF and their pins fail. The files are `tests/external/live_jira_dc/pycontribs-jira-LICENSE.txt` and `.github/schemas/gitlab-ci.schema.json`. Tests: `test_jira_dc_harness_shape`, `test_bridge_provider_wrappers`, `test_reconcile_workflow_lint`.
4. **Test harness: `_dc_fixtures.extract_store_snapshot` uses `git archive`, which applies core.autocrlf**, so extracted events come out CRLF. Test: `test_dc_store_copy_bounded_25e0` (this one reproduces on macOS too).
5. **Test: `test_mcp_publisher_pin._verify` pipes the checksum line in text mode**, so `sha256sum` sees `'mcp-publisher.tar.gz'$'\r'`.
6. **Test: `test_reclaim_bridge_history::test_unrelated_remote_ref_movement_does_not_fail_dry_run` injects its ref through a `#!/bin/sh` file named `git` on PATH.** Windows never runs it, so the ref is never created and `rev-parse` exits 128. This is not line endings; it is the shell-stub problem transhuman-wounded-pangolin solves with `tests/_exe_stub.py`.

## Approach
1. `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py`: when `text=True` and `input_data` is str:
   - Encode it with `_GIT_ENCODING`/`_GIT_ERRORS` (the codec text mode used) and run in binary mode with `check=False`.
   - Decode stdout/stderr with the same codec and subprocess's universal-newline translation (`\r\n`→`\n`, `\r`→`\n`), so returned text is identical on POSIX.
   - Only then apply `check`, raising `CalledProcessError` with the decoded str. A `TimeoutExpired` gets its `output`/`stderr` decoded the same way.
   - Apply the same in `_run_in_group`.
   - The bytes-input contract and its TypeError are unchanged.
   - `tests/unit/test_run_git_wrapper.py::test_str_input_is_forwarded_to_stdin` writes its comparison file with `write_text`, which also writes CRLF on Windows. It will write `content.encode()` with `write_bytes`, so both sides hash the same LF bytes.
2. `tier2.py`: open the alternates file with `newline="\n"`.
3. `.gitattributes`: mark the 2 vendored pinned files `-text` so no checkout converts them. Their blobs are LF today (`ls-files --eol` shows `i/lf`), so the bytes are unchanged.
4. `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py`: run `git -c core.autocrlf=false archive`.
5. `tests/unit/test_mcp_publisher_pin.py`: pipe the checksum line as bytes.
6. `test_reclaim_bridge_history.py`, `test_unrelated_remote_ref_movement_does_not_fail_dry_run`:
   - Build the ls-remote shim with pangolin's `tests/_exe_stub.py` (a Python-body stub that Windows can run) instead of a `#!/bin/sh` file.
   - Build the child environment as `{**os.environ, "PATH": os.pathsep.join([str(wrapper_dir), str(Path(git_executable).parent), os.environ.get("PATH", "")]), ...test vars}`, so the stub dir is a real first PATH entry on every OS and Windows keeps SYSTEMROOT/PATHEXT. Today the `:`-joined PATH replaces the whole environment.
   - This waits for pangolin's change on main.
- New regression tests:
  - `tests/unit/test_run_git_stdin_bytes.py`:
    - With `subprocess.run` spied, a str `input_data` reaches subprocess as encoded bytes with `text` false. The decoded stdout is unchanged (including `\r\n`→`\n`), and a failing `check=True` call raises `CalledProcessError` carrying str.
    - With `subprocess.Popen` spied, the same holds for `_run_in_group` (reached through `run_git(timeout=...)`).
  - In `test_plan_replay_tier2`, an assertion that the alternates file contains no `\r`.
- No config key, env var or flag.
- `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/crlf.args`: remove each line whose test passes in the Windows validation run. If the file ends up empty, delete it and its `@` line in `.github/workflows/test.yml`.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py
- src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier2.py
- .gitattributes
- tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_fixtures.py
- tests/unit/test_mcp_publisher_pin.py
- tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py
- tests/unit/test_run_git_stdin_bytes.py
- tests/unit/test_run_git_wrapper.py
- tests/unit/evals/test_plan_replay_tier2.py
- .github/windows-sweep-deselect/crlf.args
- .github/workflows/test.yml (only if the args file is deleted)

## Testing
- Pre-merge Windows validation on the exact fixed tree, with the lines removed: push `tmp/b4-neglectful-acceptable-gerbil`, dispatch `gh workflow run 294845723 --ref tmp/b4-neglectful-acceptable-gerbil`, and record the run id in a comment. Then delete the tmp branch.
- AC1 evidence: the first scheduled `test.yml` run on main whose head contains the merge commit. Its run id goes in a comment before the close.
- `make verify` through verify-slot.sh.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every line removed from `crlf.args` names a test that passed in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix (run id recorded in a comment).
- [ ] `crlf.args` is empty and deleted with its reference in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, or each remaining line names a test recorded on this ticket as intentionally unsupported on Windows with the reason.
